The only crossing linkage is the voice_style_guidelines concept (the section's rules apply to both voice systems), seeded below. The cut at L4482 (end of the 'Adapt length and structure' example) is clean: the next section 'Handle interruptions' begins at L4484 with its own heading.

Voice style section continued: L4484-4571 covers 'Handle interruptions gracefully' and 'Respond appropriately to audio testing'. The only crossing linkage is voice_style_guidelines (seeded below). The cut at L4571 is clean: L4572 begins a new top-level section 'Under-18 Principles'.

Under-18 Principles section: L4572-4692 covers the U18 principles (safety priorities, safety practices, declining requests, examples). The only crossing linkage is the u18_scope concept (the section applies to users ages 13-17), seeded below. The cut at L4692 is the end of the span.

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1 (L4252-4482) establishes the voice_style_guidelines concept (the section's style guidelines apply to both standard and advanced voice modes); child 2 (L4483-4571) relies on this concept for its rules about interruptions and audio testing.

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L4260 (end of voice systems intro) or L4482 (end of length/structure section); chose L4482 because the voice_style section's rules (accents, conciseness, length) are cohesive and the only crossing linkage is voice_style_guidelines. A cut at L4260 would have split the voice_style section's rules across two children, requiring more seeds.

Could have cut at L4571 (end of voice style section) instead of L4572; chose L4572 because the U18 section is a distinct top-level section with its own scope, and the cut at L4572 is clean (L4572 is the section heading).
The u18_scope concept is established and used entirely within child 3; seeded it to ensure consistency if any child needs it, though it may not cross a cut.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.

seed_vocabulary.name: voice_style_guidelines
seed_vocabulary.prose: The style guidelines in the voice_style section apply to both standard and advanced voice modes; instructions about audio/video nuances apply only to advanced voice.

seed_vocabulary.name: u18_scope
seed_vocabulary.prose: The Under-18 (U18) Principles apply to users ages 13-17 and prioritize prevention, transparency, and early intervention.
